doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Elderly band members and Clyde Bernhardt's memory
summary: Members lived to 90 and beyond; Clyde found Princess White and had remarkable recall that amazed Phil Schaap and English researchers.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now your average age has gone up since then, is that right or not?
Well not necessarily. It’s always been musicians pretty much over 60.

Well we got Fred Staton at 102, and of course Larry Lucie lived to be 101. And so that there, and then many of them got to be 90. I mean Johnny Williams was the original bass player who was in the band for 25 years. He was 90 and then he died. And Laurel Watson who was one of the singers, she was just about 90. Certainly, oh when Clyde discovered in his church in Newark the New Eden Baptist Church in Newark, he discovered Princess White, who her real name was Princess, her real name was Princess White Durrah. And he discovered her in this church. And he went up to her and he said, “Are you Princess White?” And she said yes. And then he said, “Well I remember,” she was 94 at the time and Clyde said, “I remember that in 1924, at the Lafayette Theater and I’ve forgotten what state, I delivered a telegram to you.” Because Clyde was the first black telegram boy out of Baden, South Carolina. And he said, “I delivered a telegram to you and you tipped me a dollar.” And Clyde had the best memory of anybody I’ve ever met. He was a researcher’s dream. Phil Schaap used to try to trick him. But you couldn’t. But he said, “Oh no,” Phil would say, “Well wasn’t that on December 21st?” And you said, “no it wasn’t on December 20 and you said it was on 21st.” Well Clyde would say, “Look, we went in the studio late and by the time we recorded this it was the 21st.” And he remembered everybody who was in the band when he joined it and the date that he joined, the changes that occurred in the band while he was there, and the date he left.
No. He was — Clyde played primarily with Edgar Hayes.

Yeah. Edgar Hayes and King Oliver in the 30s. And so Clyde was, I mean when I took him to England, the English guys, Lorry Wright and John Chilton and all of them, I mean they were just flabbergasted because he remembered everything. In fact there’s a book written about him called I Remember by a wonderful jazz researcher, now his name escapes me. He is deceased. He lived in Brooklyn. Oh well.
